metadata.scenario_context: A group of software engineers working remotely for a global tech company decides to initiate a team-building meeting early in January. Luis raises the idea of going on a strike to protest against some changes from the company's management.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Spain strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the possibility of scheduling the team-building meeting on January 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss a specific date for the team-building meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, I was thinking... how about we schedule the team-building meeting for January 1st? It could be a great way to start the year together. 

By the way, is it common for teams to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest? I’ve never really understood that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
January 1st... um, that’s a holiday for many. Maybe we should look at a different date, like January 3rd or 4th? 

As for strikes... in Indonesia, we generally don’t join strikes. It’s not really a common practice. We prefer to resolve issues through dialogue.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
Oh, I see... January 3rd or 4th could work too, I guess. But I still think starting on January 1st would set a positive tone. 

So, it’s not common in Indonesia. That’s interesting... but, um, why do you think some teams feel the need to protest like that? I just find it hard to understand.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
Well, you know, at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out, I guess. Some teams just have different ways of handling things. I don't really see meaningful differences here. 

But let's focus on the meeting... January 3rd or 4th would really set a better tone for the new year. What do you think about that?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
